items.title: Sonaselection India shares to list today: Check GMP ahead of debut
items.description: The Rs 141.57-crore IPO was offered in the price band of Rs 94–99 per share and comprised entirely a fresh issue of 1.43 crore equity shares, with no offer-for-sale (OFS) component.

items.title: Kheria Autocomp, SpectraA Technology Solutions SME shares to list today: Check GMP, subscription and key details
items.description: SpectraA Technology Solutions is commanding a much higher grey market premium, while Kheria Autocomp is currently trading at a relatively modest premium in the unofficial grey market. GMP figures are unofficial and unregulated and may change before listing, so they do not guarantee the actual listing price.

items.title: Positive Breakout: These 12 stocks cross above their 200 DMAs
items.description: In the Nifty500 pack, 12 stocks' closing prices crossed above their 200-day moving averages (DMA) on September 23, 2026, according to StockEdge's technical scan data. The 200-day moving average (DMA) is used by traders as a key indicator for determining the overall trend of a stock. As long as a stock's price remains above its 200-day moving average on the daily timeframe, it is generally interpreted as being in an overall uptrend.

items.title: NSE shares to list today: GMP signals 2% listing gains ahead of market debut
items.description: NSE IPO Listing time and GMP:  The Rs 22,562-crore NSE IPO comprises entirely an offer for sale (OFS) of 12.64 crore shares. Since there is no fresh issue, NSE itself will not receive any proceeds from the IPO

items.title: Hot Stocks: 3 stocks that may give returns between 16-29%
items.description: Brokerages have initiated coverage on Tata Capital, Centum Electronics, and Clean Max Enviro Energy Solutions, assigning them buy ratings. This decision is underpinned by the potential for substantial appreciation in their stock prices, with forecasts suggesting returns of 16% to 29%. Analysts point to distinct growth drivers within their sectors, reflecting a favorable outlook on their future profitability and development.

items.title: Sebi working towards balanced derivatives market: Tuhin Kanta Pandey
items.description: In a recent statement, Tuhin Kanta Pandey, the chairman of the Securities and Exchange Board of India, outlined strategic initiatives aimed at stabilizing the derivatives market. He pointed out derivatives’ vital role in bridging cash and futures trades, while recognizing that most challenges arise from short-dated index options during expiry times.

items.title: D-Street braces for weak opening on negative GIFT Nifty cues
items.description: On Wednesday, Nifty saw a notable 0.5% rise driven by widespread buying activity. Analysts are optimistic about the future of Indian equities, pointing to global influences and fluctuations in crude oil as critical factors. The market's strength was further bolstered by substantial purchases from foreign institutional investors, although the rupee struggled against the US dollar due to a robust dollar and escalating crude oil prices.

items.title: Stocks in news: Bharat Dynamics, NTPC, Canara Bank and Waaree Energies
items.description: Indian equity benchmarks experienced gains on Wednesday, driven by widespread buying in the market. Investors reacted positively to signs of potential de-escalation in West Asia and changing crude oil prices. The Nifty 50 and Sensex indices both increased after assessing recent corporate developments and strategic forecasts. Key stocks including Bharat Dynamics and NTPC are anticipated to remain in focus following significant announcements.

items.title: Morgan Stanley's Asia deal plans leaked in staffer's email misfire
items.description: A Morgan Stanley staffer inadvertently shared an internal document listing more than 100 investment deals. The leaked list included potential initial public offerings in Asia, along with private equity partners and suspended projects. The incident arose from an email sent this week, which the staffer attempted to retract later. Morgan Stanley stated it takes client confidentiality seriously and addressed the information leak immediately.

items.title: SBI expects surplus from new UPI MDR as issuing, acquiring bank
items.description: State Bank of India will start charging a merchant discount rate on UPI payments exceeding Rs 2,000 from October 15. The bank anticipates generating surplus revenue due to its extensive card issuing and payment gateway services. Initially, MDR fees will be divided among issuing and acquiring banks, payment gateways, and UPI applications. SBI is evaluating the potential impact of transaction splitting on its systems and volumes.

items.title: HSBC plans India equity broking return after 13 years amid IPO boom, sources say
items.description: After a decade-long hiatus, HSBC is gearing up to re-enter the Indian equity broking sector, responding to the increasing demands from wealthy clients and an active share sale market. The bank is set to introduce retail broking services shortly, leveraging its existing broking license. With this move, HSBC aims to enhance its equities platform and tap into the growing retail investor segment in India’s wealth management landscape.

items.title: NSE IPO: India's biggest exchange lists at ₹1,800 per share; gains 5% after flat debut
items.description: India's largest stock exchange operator recorded a subdued trading debut Thursday, opening around one percent higher than its issue price after raising $2.35 billion in the country's second-biggest initial public offering. The National Stock Exchange (NSE), which handles the vast majority of domestic equities trading, has been one of India's most anticipated listings this year and comes after a decade-long wait to go public. Shares opened at 1,800 rupees ($18.7) on rival exchange BSE, up just 0.84 percent from the IPO price of 1,785 rupees, before rising further to hit 1,861.85 rupees in morning trade.

items.title: Stocks to buy: UBS picks 4 NBFC shares with upside potential of up to 36%
items.description: UBS expects India to enter a strong unsecured credit growth cycle, led by personal loans. The brokerage said this is supported by healthy asset quality across banks and NBFCs, flat unsecured household leverage over the past three years, ample system liquidity and a more risk-on approach among lenders. Here are 4 stocks that the brokerage is bullish on:

items.title: PB Fintech loses Rs 22,700 cr from market value as stock crashes 26% after IRDAI’s reform plans. What Citi and Jefferies are warning
items.description: PB Fintech shares plunged 26%, wiping out nearly Rs 22,703 crore from its market capitalisation after IRDAI proposed changes to insurance commission structures. Jefferies flagged risks to distributor earnings, while Citi warned of a potential sharp compression in distribution economics across several high-margin insurance categories.

items.title: Sebi board meeting: PMS rules overhaul, FPI commodity trades among key decisions to watch out
items.description: Sebi's upcoming board meeting aims to discuss significant changes to portfolio management services and settlement regulations. Proposed revisions could allow discretionary portfolio managers to make new types of investments, including overseas assets. The meeting is expected to review widening the accredited investor framework to increase market participation. Another key focus is enhancing foreign portfolio investor access in commodity derivatives to improve liquidity.

items.title: Multibagger trap: 15 stocks that soared up to 4,000% in 2025 crashed as much as 90%
items.description: In 2025, numerous stocks saw remarkable growth, but the following year revealed a stark contrast in their trajectories. While Cupid enjoyed impressive gains, Blue Pearl Agriventures suffered considerable losses. This shift indicates a more cautious market with heightened selectivity in stock performance, driven by varying global economic factors that heavily impact investor choices and market predictions.

items.title: NSE draws brokerage attention on stock market debut as 3 firms initiate coverage on Day 1
items.description: NSE shares rallied after a muted listing at Rs 1,800, pushing the exchange into India’s ninth-most valued company with a market cap of Rs 4.63 lakh crore. The post-listing surge came as three major brokerages initiated coverage on Day 1 with positive ratings. Macquarie called NSE “The Dominator” and assigned an Outperform rating with a Rs 1,965 target price.

items.title: Avantel shares rise 9% after Rs 177 crore satellite communication order from Zetwerk
items.description: Avantel shares jumped over 8% on Thursday after securing a Rs 177.35 crore purchase order from Zetwerk Manufacturing Businesses for satellite communication equipment. Scheduled for execution by March 2027, the domestic manufacturing contract boosts revenue visibility for the telecom and defence electronics manufacturer following robust Q1 FY27 results.

items.title: NSE becomes 9th most valued company with Rs 4.63 lakh crore m-cap after IPO. Who did it overtake?
items.description: The National Stock Exchange (NSE) made a rather modest entrance on the Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE), opening at Rs 1,800 against its IPO price of Rs 1,785. With a market capitalization of Rs 4.63 lakh crore, it has emerged as the ninth largest entity in India. Analysts predict that shares may fluctuate due to early trading demand-supply movements.

items.title: PB Fintech among 4 F&O stocks with a sharp rise in futures open interest
items.description: As of September 23, four stocks in the NSE F&O segment recorded a rise of more than 10% in futures open interest compared with the previous trading session. A notable increase in futures open interest indicates a substantial rise in the number of active, unexpired futures contracts in a security. This can reflect market participants initiating new positions or increasing the size of existing positions.

items.title: Steel Authority of India among 3 stocks showing White Marubozu pattern
items.description: On September 23, three stocks in the Nifty 500 pack that gained over 5% appeared on the ‘White Marubozu’ bullish scanner, according to technical scan data from StockEdge. A White Marubozu is a bullish candlestick pattern in technical analysis that occurs when the opening price is the lowest for a given period and the closing price is the highest.The pattern is represented by a long white (or green) candlestick with no upper shadow and little or no lower shadow. It reflects strong upward price movement during the session, with the price moving from the opening level toward the session high by the close. The pattern is commonly studied in technical analysis as an indicator of price momentum.

items.title: Didn’t get NSE IPO shares? Should you buy after listing, wait for a dip or bet on BSE?
items.description: NSE Shares: As the National Stock Exchange (NSE) emerges on the market, investors are presented with various investment avenues. Options include buying shares, waiting for strategic price dips, or exploring the rival BSE. Experts advise thorough assessment of market fluctuations and valuations. Long-term investors should consider a gradual approach to accumulating shares, taking into account NSE's dominance, while still evaluating BSE’s promising prospects and operational frameworks.

items.title: NSE shares jump 5% after muted debut, market value swells by Rs 19,290 crore. Why Macquarie, other brokerages are bullish
items.description: NSE Share Price: National Stock Exchange shares made their market debut at Rs 1,800, which is slightly above the IPO price. The listing reflects a market capitalization exceeding Rs 4.45 lakh crore, significantly higher than BSE's Rs 1.33 lakh crore. The IPO aimed to raise Rs 22,562 crore through an offer for sale of shares by existing shareholders. Additionally, the shares had a grey market premium of 2% before listing.

items.title: Bharat Dynamics shares rise 2% in a weak market after bagging Rs 811 crore order from Ministry of Defence
items.description: Bharat Dynamics shares gained 2% after the Defence Ministry awarded an Rs 810.79-crore contract for 160 SAT-SAAW weapons and associated equipment for the Indian Air Force, adding to the company’s order visibility amid rising defence spending.

items.title: Why is market falling today? Sensex tumbles over 850 points, Nifty below 23,150. 5 factors behind D-St rout
items.description: The Indian stock market fell significantly as Sensex and Nifty dropped over 1%. The downturn was driven by surging US bond yields, which reached a 19-year high. Expectations of a rate hike by the Federal Reserve added to market concerns and uncertainty. Furthermore, rising oil prices displaced investor confidence amid ongoing geopolitical tensions. Analysts suggest that continued volatility is likely, depending on global economic developments.

items.title: IFCI, New India Assurance, other stocks drop up to 3% as NSE makes a muted market debut. What to expect?
items.description: On Thursday, shares of IFCI, New India Assurance Company, and General Insurance Corporation fell up to 3%. The National Stock Exchange listed with less than a 1% premium over the IPO price. NSE's initial public offering aimed to raise Rs 22,562 crore entirely through an offer for sale. Analysts anticipated long-term potential for NSE despite the muted listing, with a target price of Rs 1,965.
